I am in favour of this ruling for the simple reason that it undoes a particularly troubling precedent. As long as LGBT individuals were denied certain invaluable rights afforded to the straight majority, them it creates a precedent for denying them other essential freedoms as well. As long as this right of union was not afforded to these people on the basis of who they are wired to love, then it makes it ever so slightly easier to deny them other essential freedoms as well. The decision made by the U.S. Supreme Court today goes quite a long way towards fully undoing that precedent.

Now for a bit of context on what I am about to say, I am a closeted bisexual male of English birth and British nationality. I speak not as one involved in what has just occurred in America, but as an outsider saddened to see the majority of commentators reducing this human triumph to a cynical political manoeuvre. There is much more to it than that.

Now, assuming you are capable of basic human empathy, which I somewhat doubt, put yourself in my shoes for a minute. Imagine reaching puberty and becoming acutely aware of your alienation from your straight peers. Imagine struggling to come to terms with what you are while society does everything to imply that you are an abombnation and a freak simply for being outside the norm. Then imagine coming to this comment thread, and seeing the people of Voat decide at once that the struggle of anyone outside their little bubble doesn't matter.

And to see you unable to acknowledge this simple fact saddens me greatly.

So what if it's only a small percentage of the population that benefits from this? This is still a maligned collection of minorities finally getting a good chunk of the way to full equality, not only legally but societally. Sure, the number is small, but the difference between 0 and 1 is as vast as the difference between one and infinity. A single voice singing out to the darkness is infinitely greater than a total forlorn silence. And until the day where every misfit toy of the human race gets to sing together in sheer joy of their essential humanity, I'll keep hoping.

And if people like you don't like that, then maybe you should look in a mirror and get a good look at the parts of you that can't be seen, all the little beliefs and preconceptions that you hold inside you without any serious thought.
